title: perf-canary: adaptive auto-detection + hysteresis rollout guards
author: Priya Desai
description: Context: Our performance canary system has been generating noisy alerts for transient latency spikes and small KV-cache-related variance. This PR implements adaptive auto-detection for regressions and a hysteresis-based rollout guard to reduce false positives and avoid unnecessary rollbacks during transient load patterns. Motivation: Reduce human intervention on canary rollouts while keeping safety for customer-facing traffic. Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive detector: perf-canary/detector.py adds an adaptive baseline model that weights recent percentiles and traffic mix to compute dynamic thresholds per route and model. 2) Hysteresis module: perf-canary/hysteresis.py implements stateful hysteresis for the detector so that a single spike does not trigger a rollback; thresholds require sustained violation over a configured window. 3) KV-aware thresholds: detector integrates KV-cache hit-rate signals (perf-canary/kv_metrics_collector.py) so thresholds relax during expected cache churn. 4) Rollout guards: pkg/deploy/rollout_guard.go adds guard hooks to the orchestrator to pause or abort traffic shifts based on hysteresis state and aggregated SLA metrics. 5) Observability: metrics/dashboard.json and docs/perf-canary.md updated with new metrics, SLOs, and recommended alert thresholds. 6) IaC: infra/alerts.tf adds new alerting policies and onboarding script for SRE. 7) Tests: tests/perf_canary_integration_test.py exercise the end-to-end detection logic with synthetic traffic and KV churn scenarios. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves the previous static-threshold detector when the adaptive detector is disabled by config; rollout guard defaults to conservative settings to avoid accidental blocking. Migration: cluster config needs the new perf_canary.feature_flag and an optional per-service config block (docs updated). Related: ENG-2741 (noise reduction), ENG-2810 (kv-aware thresholds).

review_comments: Marco: Can you elaborate on how the adaptive baseline responds to sustained traffic shifts (e.g., new model rollout)? Priya: The detector uses an exponential decay window and a traffic-mix weight so sustained shifts over the calibration window (default 30m) will move the baseline upward; we also provide an opt-in fast-track mode to seed the baseline when known good performance metrics are supplied. Courtney: The hysteresis thresholds look reasonable but we should avoid long windows for latency-sensitive routes. Requested change: make per-route window configurable and default to 3 consecutive evaluation windows for critical routes. Priya: Applied, added per-route overrides and documented the defaults. Ethan: Integration tests look solid; please ensure CI has a reproducible RNG seed for synthetic traffic. Priya: Fixed and re-ran tests. release_notes:
- perf-canary: adaptive auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions (opt-in via feature flag)
- perf-canary: hysteresis-based rollout guards to reduce noisy aborts and unnecessary rollbacks
- perf-canary: KV-cache aware thresholds to prevent false positives during cache churn
- Added dashboards and SLO guidance; updated docs and onboarding
testing: Unit tests: added for detector math, hysteresis state transitions. Integration: synthetic traffic harness simulating steady traffic, bursty traffic, and KV cache churn. Perf canary benchmarks: run end-to-end on perf-canary-lab with 10k synthetic requests; ROC false-positive rate down from ~9% to ~2% on historical traces when adaptive detector enabled. Manual verification: SRE ran a staged canary against dedicated cluster, observed expected pause behavior when sustained regression occurred.
rollout_plan: Default rollout: enable feature flag in main, start canary at 1% traffic for 15 minutes, if no sustained violations escalate to 10% for 30 minutes, then progressive 25%->50%->100% with health checks. Hysteresis: require 3 consecutive evaluation windows (window=5m) before triggering abort for latency-sensitive routes; non-critical routes default to 2 windows. Operators can adjust per-service thresholds via perf_canary_config.yaml. Alerts: SRE will be notified on pause/abort events and can manually resume after investigation.
